# My Journey

I used to preach [Buddhist enlightenment](http://mindset.u-dont-exist.com/) a lot. Then I noticed I could feel spiritually free and still turn right back into the same little kid when an old wound got hit. Whatever had become free in me hadn't reached that kid. I started thinking most people who chase spiritual freedom are partly trying to get above childhood pain, or get away from parts of ourselves we don't want to meet. That's [spiritual bypassing](https://goenka.u-dont-exist.com/). I think plenty of seekers and gurus do it too; I've written about the [Dalai Lama as one example](https://substack.com/@udontexist/note/c-245314772?r=5vdc6m).

The way I picture it is almost stupidly simple. Imagine you're broke and starving, and your baby is starving too. *Understandable*: there is no food. Then a food bank opens nearby and suddenly you've got lots of nutritious munchies. But you're eating all of it yourself while baby you is still starving. *Unforgivable.*

Nobody would knowingly leave a baby starving. I just didn't think the baby was really there. Until a few years ago, inner-child stuff sounded pretty silly to me. Then I started to feel him directly. Once that happened, it was hard not to notice that I'd found all this love and freedom and was still leaving him out.

I don't think people bypass because they're stupid or crazy. I did it too. I just didn't know there was anyone there to bring the love to. Reparenting only started making sense after the child felt real to me. Then there was actually a little me there who was hurting.

I don't want therapy to become my whole life, either. If all I'm doing is processing childhood pain, I'm still spending my life on childhood pain. Spirituality showed me my life story wasn't the limit of how much love or happiness I could know. Maybe ordinary life already gives you enough love and meaning. It didn't for me. Love that depended on conditions never felt like enough, and I couldn't stop wondering whether there was something deeper.

### Don’t Give the Inner Adult Away

If you still feel like a kid inside, someone who seems genuinely grown-up can have way too much power. You feel small, they seem to know how life works, and some part of you wants to say: okay, you drive. Sometimes you do need that. Let somebody carry one grown-up thing with you while you learn how to do it yourself. I call that borrowed adulthood. The problem is when they never start handing it back.

When you feel that small, it's easy to assume the grown-up must know better. But a helper can see something you can't see and still be wrong about you. Even [Pema Chödrön](https://pemachodronfoundation.org/product/taking-the-leap-book/) comes from a tradition where devotion to a teacher is a big deal, and she still says a teacher should “wean us from dependency altogether” and help us grow up.

If your actual life is unsafe, the kid doesn't need a better meditation technique. They need you to deal with the thing that's actually happening. That may mean getting out or getting help. Spiritual practice may change how the pain feels, but it can't make danger safe. Calling real danger merely “your story” leaves the child alone with it.

No-self teachings can hit like a trap if you grew up learning that what you wanted didn't matter. You're finally trying to find out what you want and what you believe, and to discover that you can actually say no. Then somebody tells you there is no you. Maybe that teaching becomes freeing later. But you may need enough of a self to stand somewhere first. Otherwise “there is no self” can become another way to disappear.

Therapy can do this too. If I say, “No, this doesn't feel right for me,” the other person has to leave open the possibility that I'm right. Maybe they're wrong about me. Maybe their method is going somewhere I don't want to go. If every no becomes “resistance,” then I don't actually get to say no. I want to be able to disagree and still make my own decision without needing the therapist to certify it. I want to need them less over time. Borrow adulthood. Do not surrender it.

My own case was weird. I was well-loved as a child, but from age twelve to twenty-six I was depressed and cried every night from feeling the pain of the world. [Loving-kindness (metta) meditation](http://love.u-dont-exist.com/) healed that depression almost instantly for me.

I wasn't lacking love. My parents had given me a lot of it. I found more in [Buddhist teachings—which, it turns out, also include inner-child self-love!](https://substack.com/profile/355021294-u-dont-existcom/note/c-297324975) and later in [loveyhuasca](http://soma.u-dont-exist.com/). Metta gave all that love somewhere to land.

But it didn't reach everything. A lot of the child stuff around my attachment to women was still there. When I later tried [self-directed inner-child therapy](https://youtu.be/yEWFjODXJbI?si=IXUqrhExojOm6Itm), it felt like I was making it up at first. I used San Pedro cactus and CBD tea with sublingual mapacho, and that cracked it open; structured sessions with an inner-child therapist deepened it.

“Find the wounded child and love them” sounded simple until I tried it. Sometimes a protective part wouldn't let me near the child. Other times I was so completely the child that there was no grown-up me around to do those three adult jobs. Borrowed adulthood came out of that second problem.
